sections.text: I long to see Thee as thou wert before, with the crown, the sceptre and the discus in Thy hands; in Thy other Form, with Thy four hands, O Thou Whose arms are countless and Whose forms are infinite.

Lord Shri Krishna replied: My beloved friend! It is only through My grace and power that thou hast been able to see this vision of splendour, the Universal, the Infinite, the Original. Never has it been seen by any but thee.
Not by study of the scriptures, not by sacrifice or gift, not by ritual or rigorous austerity, is it possible for man on earth to see what thou hast seen, O thou foremost hero of the Kuru-clan!

So far we have discussed chapter 11. As we always try to remind ourselves, this chapter is all about the cosmic form of the Lord. Cosmic form of the Lord means the cosmic form of my own self -- the self which I know since I became aware of myself as this me. When that paradigm shifts and I see that as the all-pervading self, thats the paradigm shift that happened for Arjuna. We learn all this through the scriptures and religions and philosophy -- that there is a unity in this diversity -- but it is very hard to comprehend. And therefore we crave to have that experience of that unity.
And Arjuna vocalizes our urge to see that unity to Krishna and said, I understand all that, but I want to experience it. I want to see that form of yours, O Supreme Lord, that I can understand all of that. And Bhagawan said, Ill show you. You wont be able to see it through your normal perception. The normal perception we have is I and the world exists. And therefore there is a duality.
There is a constant struggle between I and the world, where I define myself as me and the world as everything else. And then this world we divide into two: the world which I like and the world which I dont like. So our whole life pursuit is to align with the world which I like and avoid the world which I dont like. Vedanta says, all of life, the pursuit is to avoid what is unpleasant and to gain what is pleasant. And this pursuit creates the friction, and that creates more unhappiness, more dissatisfaction, because almost everyone around me is trying to do the same thing. And then we are in competition to get out of that race. If I can get that vision of oneness, then I can have that everlasting peace that I am seeking.
So Bhagavan showed this roop to Arjuna. And Arjuna sees this world without any space and time. The dividing factor between I and the world is the space and time. And once that is taken off, I see this world as one entity ever strung into each other by a common thread. But this is an overwhelming picture for Arjuna. So he said, Im delighted to see this, but at the same time I am completely overwhelmed and Im fearful.
So oh Lord, show me your form which is much gentler and which I am most comfortable with, which is that of Vishnu. We want to see Bhagavan in a form which is most comfortable to us, as we have discussed last time. So he says, show me with your form with the Kiritinam Gadinam, Chakrinam Hastam, with the crown and mace and Chakra which Im so familiar with. Right from my childhood Ive seen Vishnus pictures and anytime somebody says, have you seen cosmic form? All of us say, oh yes, yeah, Ive seen Bhagavad Gita pictures and you know, Shiva. Sure, because we have seen all the paintings of Shiva.
So we had a familiarity. We have formed an image of God in our head, and any image other than that -- the whole understanding that this Almighty is nothing but the source of all these beings and is all these beings -- is not really a comforting thought. Therefore, very conveniently, we divide the world into good and bad. Everything good happening is divine; bad happening is evil. Tsunami is evil, earthquake is evil. But in reality, its all part of the whole phenomenon called this world. Theres nothing evil or good about it.
Arjuna asked for that, and then Bhagavan said in his response -- maya prasannena tava Arjuna, Idam Rupam Param Darsitam, Atma Yogat -- the last verse which we have seen. He said, I showed you the supreme form of mine graciously, because you are my devoted student, a friend, and a devotee. With my yoga, with my power of changing your perception, I have showed you my form. Not that this form was never available. It is always available to those who can see it. Radio waves are always here for those who can tune into them -- the fact that were not tuning into them doesnt mean theyre not there. The form was always there. Arjuna did not have the capacity to see it. But my yoga gave you that perception which was Tejomayam Vishwam, Anantam, Adyam, Yanme tvad anyena Drishta Purvam -- the splendid and all-encompassing Vishwam, all-pervading infinite form which you have seen and not seen by any other before. Now, there are some saying thats not true -- Krishna already showed it to Yashoda. This is not an argument about the Puranas saying, who saw it first?
The point is that no one in this state of mind, state of evolution, state of understanding has seen this thing. If I say, Well, I actually saw it while driving down to work yesterday -- well, thats not true, not going to happen. Because then I wont be able to drive, because I lose that whole perception of the road, my car, and me as separate. I cant have these two together -- the perception of me and this world as separate, and the perception of me and the world as one and the same -- both at the same time.
Therefore I say, nobody has seen it before you, you remaining you. Arjuna has seen this form. And then why this is not seen by others? Because others are trying to see this by the means which they find most convenient and appropriate. We are also trying to find that source of happiness which has infinite power to make us happy. So we try our own way.
We say we will have the best education. We want our children to be the happiest in this world. What are we going to do? Were going to make sure they go to the best schools, well make sure they have the best health care, will make sure they will have the best desk. But do they really turn out to be the best as we see it? Because what they are looking for, or lets put it this way, we think we have done the best for them to make them happy.
Does it make them happy? In fact, half the time what we have done to make them happy makes them most unhappy. But thats the only means which we know to transfer happiness to someone else.
Na Veda Yajna Adhyayanair Na Danair Na Cha Kriyabhir Na Tapobhir Ugraih. All others are trying in this world -- by the Veda, by Dhyana, by learning Vedas. We want to learn. When I was a teenager and I see people talking about Bhagavad Gita and I used to say, I understand nothing, but someday I really want to know what theyre talking about.
So we want to get the knowledge which we think the others have. So we learn Veda, Yajna, all the things which we think is good. With doing Dana, I remember in my childhood when Surat, when there is eclipse, everybody comes out in a street and then the beggars come and they know that now theres a big business time because people are doing dana at that time. Because if you do that it multiplies so many times. So Dana -- we obviously value the importance of charity. We have this notion that doing Dana, I get the merits, and that merit will earn me the vision of that source of infinite happiness, the Lord.
Yajna, Dhyana, Dana, Kriyabhi. Now actions -- obviously they translate as rituals, because religious actions in the traditional sense means ritual. I have to do this Archana or I have to do this Puja because that gives me merits, or do austerities or fasts. This many on this day, that many on that day -- all this. We are doing it to ultimately find that source of happiness which is infinite. I want that unconditioned happiness, unending happiness.
And I want to do that by gaining this. Bhagavan very clearly says, na veda na kriyabhi na tapobhi. Its not that Bhagavan is condemning this. Somewhat in a putting-it-down tone, I said this -- thats not the intention. Those are the means to prepare your mind and intellect to a level where he will shine through. We have discussed that a seekers job is only to do the Antahkarana Shuddhi.
As per our Vedanta, our job is simply to make our Antahkarana -- the internal instrument, which is mind and intellect -- to clean it up, make it ready for his reflection into it. Because right now it is so clouded with all the layers of our vasanas on it that the reflection is not clear. We have seen in Vedanta that three types of impurities can be there. The first is like smoke in front of a mirror. You cant see the reflection because there is smoke in front of the mirror.
Well, it is very easy to dispel the smoke. But then there is the dust layer on the mirror. And third, we say, just as in the womb the fetus is enveloped in matter -- which is even more difficult. Our job with this mind and its impurities is simply to clean up the impurities. All this we have discussed is actually just for the Antahkarana Shuddhi.
Veda, Dhyana, Yajna, Tapa, Dana, Kriya -- all that is for Antahkarana Shuddhi. If you are doing it for Antahkarana Shuddhi, it will gain its results. This is all I have to do, and Im done with it. And therefore he says, you are not getting it through these alone. So Bhagavan says, evam rupah sakya aham nrloke --
this form of mine is not possible to be seen in this world of man. Drastum tvad anyena kuru pravira -- Arjuna is Kuru Pravira, the best among the Kurus. It is not possible in this world for anyone other than you to see this by these means alone, because these are the means and not the end -- which we normally confuse as the end. The next verse we just saw is Ma te vyatha. This is a verse which shows what state Arjuna was in. Ma te vyatha cha vimudhabhavah --
Dont be disturbed and dont be fearful. I can see clearly on your face that you are disturbed, overwhelmed, and fearful by looking at this terrible form of mine. Drishtva rupam ghoram idrik mama idam -- having seen such a terrible form of mine. See, again, somewhere in the translation it says terrific form. But it says Ghoram, which means terrible. Whether it is terrible or terrific -- who decides that?
From our point of view something may be terrible. From some other perspective it is terrific when somebody is taking those pictures of tsunamis from a distance from some satellite and then we are seeing those such a terrific form of tsunami. But guy at that whatever the beach where the tsunami is coming in Japan or wherever that is, its a terrible form of tsunami. So he says, having seen this terrible form of mine -- because you are seeing it as a jiva, as a limited being, trying to comprehend this overwhelming nature of the self -- its a terrible form. Vyapetabhih pritamanah -- with your fear dispelled, get your fear out, and pritamanah, have a loving nature again. Punastvam tadeva me rupam idam prapashya.
And now see this form which will remove your fear -- a loving form. Now comes a little bit of a controversy. When Bhagavan came back from his Virat Swarupa, what form did he show? Arjuna had asked for Kiritinam Gadinam Chakrinam Hastam -- you know, Vishnu Roop. But Bhagavad Gita really doesnt say that. Some commentaries have said Bhagavad Gita simply says he came back to his original gentle form as Vasudev Krishna.

Krishna grants Arjunas request to see a gentler form, then makes a remarkable statement: Never has it been seen by any but thee... Not by study of the scriptures, not by sacrifice or gift, not by ritual or rigorous austerity, is it possible for man on earth to see what thou hast seen. This seems to negate all spiritual practice - if study, sacrifice, charity, and austerity cannot grant this vision, what can? The answer lies in what these practices prepare us for rather than what they directly achieve.
The teaching here parallels success in any field. Going to architecture school does not guarantee becoming a successful architect - many graduates never practice. The training is necessary but not sufficient. What is also required is devotion and the grace of opportunities. Similarly, spiritual practices purify the mind and prepare us, but the actual vision comes through grace - it cannot be demanded or earned.
For todays practice, examine your relationship to spiritual effort. Are you treating practices as transactions - I did this much meditation, so I deserve that much peace? Or are you doing practices for their own sake, to purify and prepare, while remaining open to grace? The vision comes through grace, in its own time, to those who have prepared and remained humble. Today, do your practices with full effort and zero expectation. Offer the effort itself as worship, and release all claims to results.
